title: יוֹנָה נִכְאָבָה | Yonah Nikhavah — reshut №6 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Divrei, by Yehudah ha-Levi
author: Isaac Gantwerk Mayer (transcription & naqdanut)

coauthors.name: Yehudah ben Shmuel haLevi
coauthors.bio: Yehudah haLevi (also Judah ha-Levi; Hebrew: יהודה הלוי and Judah ben Shmuel Halevi יהודה בן שמואל הלוי; Arabic: يهوذا اللاوي‎; c. 1075 – 1141) was a Spanish Jewish physician, poet and philosopher. He was born in Spain, either in Toledo or Tudela, in 1075 or 1086, and died shortly after arriving in the Holy Land in 1141, at that point the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem. Yehudah haLevi is considered one of the greatest Hebrew poets, celebrated both for his religious and secular poems, many of which appear in present-day liturgy. His greatest philosophical work was The Kuzari.

content:
In older Sephardic practice, there are cycles of reshuyot (permission-poems) recited on the three sabbaths of rebuke. These reshuyot, inserted before important prayers, date back to medieval Andalusian poets. They are largely mournful in tone, and accordingly the Ḥida opposed their recitation as unbefitting the joy of sabbaths, but due to their antiquity and cherishedness some communities (for instance those of Morocco) preserved them, reciting them all prior to Maariv on the ninth of Av instead. In any case, they are very clearly designed for the Shabbatot to which they are assigned, and to serve as reshuyot for the prayers to which they are assigned.

This reshut, by Yehuda haLevi, is the sixth of six reshuyot for the first sabbath of rebuke, Shabbat Divrei, the first Sabbath of Rebuke after 17 Tammuz. It is recited before the Torah Service after the public repetition of the Shaḥarit Amidah.

Source (Hebrew) Translation (English)
יוֹנָה נִכְאָבָה
נַפְשָׁהּ דָּאֲבָה
הֵיכַל דָּר עֲרָבוֹת
יוֹם יוֹם סוֹבְבָה׃
The dove[1] Israel  aches;
her soul grieves away
turning to the Cloud-Dweller’s palace
day after day!
הוֹמִיָּה בְּקוֹלָהּ תִּתְחַנֵּן לְדוֹד
נוֹדַע כִּי בְּכִסְלָהּ הִרְבָּה הַנְּדֹד
לוּ הִתְעַגְּבָה עַל־דָּת דַּהֲבָא
כְּאִישׁוֹן וּבָנוֹת צוּרַת הַשָּׁבָה׃
יוֹנָה נִכְאָבָה…
Murmuring with her voice, she petitions her Amour,
Knowing that her folly made the tossed exile more.
Would that she desire her golden faith in the way
of a pupil or daughters, to return and stay!
The dove aches…
הַבַּת הַיְקָרָה קוּמִי־נָא שְׁבִי
יִפְעַת־לָךְ נְהוֹרָא לָךְ בַּת־הַצְּבִי
עָבְרָה הָעֶבְרָה לֹא־תִּהְיֶה שְׁבִי
כִּי כׇּל־מֵי שְׁבָא גַּם מֵימֵי סְבָא
לֹ֤א יֽוּכְלוּ֙ לְכַבּ֣וֹת אֶת־הָֽאַהֲבָ֔ה׃
יוֹנָה נִכְאָבָה…
Cherished daughter, rise, please, stay here, don’t go!
Brightness is yours, splendid daughter, you are aglow!
Wrath has passed, no more of your captivity’s woe.
For all the waters of Sheva and Seva’s[2] Two associated nations, mentioned in Psalms 72:10. Likely somewhere around modern-day Yemen or Somalia, and thus associated with Islam. Yehuda haLevi famously took a lengthy ocean voyage to reach the land of Israel.  oceans of spray
Could not quench the fire of love away.
The dove aches…
